design: Weak situations show preferences best: situational-strength theory (Mischel 1977; Meyer, Dalal & Hermida 2010 meta-analysis) finds traits predict behaviour most where roles and rules are loose. Hobbies, taste and friendships are freely chosen and lightly scripted, unlike work/study (w, l-with-obligations) or Thai family life (r) with its seniority and กตัญญู norms. So these contexts add exactly the low-press observations a preference model needs, and cut the 'Te/Si because the job demands it' artefact.

Hobbies (f): leisure-personality research links leisure choice and style to personality (Kirkcaldy & Furnham 1991; Barnett 2006; Stebbins' 'serious leisure' with its career-like stages). How people pick up, practise, collect and quit a hobby gives clean process data for the perceiving functions: Se learns hands-on, Si by repetition and reference memory, Ne by recombining, Ni by converging on a core. The f bank exploits this well (Sef1, Sif1, Nef0, Nif1).

Taste (q): Openness to Aesthetics (NEO O2) is the Big Five facet nearest to taste, and MBTI S–N correlates about .7 with Openness (McCrae & Costa 1989; Furnham 1996). Gosling et al. (2002, 'A Room with a Cue') showed that bedrooms and offices reliably reveal Openness and Conscientiousness to observers, and Rentfrow & Gosling (2003) tied music taste to personality. That backs decor and dress items as valid function cues: Teq0/Teq4 (system, decluttering) vs Fiq1 (meaningful non-matching objects) vs Niq1 (one overall feel).

Friends (x): friendship is voluntary and less hierarchical than Thai family, so judging functions are less masked by filial duty. Personality predicts friendship formation and support style (Asendorpf & Wilpers 1998; Selfhout et al. 2010). The bank's conflict and support items (Tix1/Fex2/Tex4/Fix3 on 'a friend asks for advice or two friends fight') put all four judging functions in one shared scenario, which is the ideal set-up for MFC.

Forced-choice payoff: matched-desirability MFC resists faking better than Likert (Cao & Drasgow 2019 meta-analysis; Christiansen et al. 2005). Three new everyday contexts mean more same-context candidates, so the 0.5→0.75→1.0 ladder will relax less often. My ratings put the new contexts' means near target (f≈3.40, q≈3.41, x≈3.43), with tight per-function spreads apart from a few Fe/helper outliers.

Pitfall 1: social desirability in x and f. In Thai collectivist culture (เกรงใจ, น้ำใจ) helping, hosting and sacrificing for the group are top virtues, and a 'แม้ตัวเองจะ…' sacrifice clause RAISES desirability rather than lowering it. I rate Sex1, Tex1, Tix4, Fix4 and Fef1 at 3.8–3.9. Use costs that are mildly awkward (Te solution-mode, Ti interrogating, Fi seen as too serious), not self-sacrificing.

Pitfall 2: confounds. (a) E/I: group-chat, meetup and 'ลุย' items drift toward Extraversion, so keep Fe ≠ sociable and Se ≠ thrill (fix Sex2, BNiSex1). (b) Openness halo: Ne/Ni taste items can read as 'creative/deep', so Si/Se need their own aesthetic dignity (Siq4 and Seq4 do this well). (c) Money/class: gear, brands and owning a room presuppose resources; keep items doable on a small budget or in a shared room, and avoid gendered dress or decor examples.

Pitfall 3: redundancy and local dependence. Gift choice repeats across q/x, group trips across j/x, and gear across f/u. The incubation script for Ni is used 7+ times, and BNiSeq0 copies Niq1 vs Seq3. Near-duplicates in one session inflate inter-item dependence, which already strains ipsative scoring (Brown & Maydeu-Olivares 2011). Have the engine block same-idea pairs within a session, and pilot-check that f/q/x scores load with the same function from other contexts (convergent r) before trusting them.
